title: Revamp build profiles and introduce dependency curation pipeline
author: Ethan Morales
release_notes:
- Introduces explicit build profiles (dev/ci/release/minimal) to standardize build artifacts and caching.
- Adds a dependency curation pipeline that proactively groups, tests, and proposes safe upgrades.
- Splits lint and unit smoke checks into fast lanes to speed PR feedback.
- No breaking API changes; runtime behavior unchanged.
description:
Context: Our monorepo has accumulated ad-hoc build artifacts and CI wiring that slows feedback and causes cache churn. This PR introduces a formal set of build profiles (dev/ci/release/minimal) plus a dependency curation pipeline (dep-curator) that reduces noisy dependency churn and groups upgrades for safer testing. Motivation: reduce CI noise, speed fast-path feedback, and reduce flakiness from transitive updates.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Add 'build/profiles/' with Dockerfile fragments and canonical build args for each profile (dev, ci, release, minimal).
- Update .github/workflows/ci.yml to drive different lanes based on profile and changed paths; introduce a fast-lane for lint+unit-smoke and a heavier lane for integration and release-preview.
- Add a new action 'tools/dep-curator' which runs nightly to evaluate dependency deltas, run batched test matrices against candidate upgrades, and open curated PRs with grouped changes.
- Introduce 'toolchain-resolver' step that pins node/go/python per-project using a central lockfile so builds are hermetic.
- Split lint into language-specific jobs (ts-lint, go-lint, python-lint) and moved typecheck into a separate cache-warmed job to prevent CLs from being blocked by unrelated flakiness.
- Add docs: build/profiles/README.md and docs/ci/dep-curation.md with migration steps for platform teams.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add build profile artifacts and docs
- [x] CI workflow: fast-lane + de-duped cache keys
- [x] Implement dep-curator action and onboarding job
- [x] Add staged smoke integration job for release previews
- [x] Update Makefile and repo-level scripts to honor profile flags
- [x] Add migration guide for infra and SDK owners

Migration notes: Small teams should opt into 'ci' profile by exporting PROFILE=ci in their build scripts. Release pipelines are unaffected unless explicitly switched to 'release' profile. Dep-curator runs in preview mode for 2 weeks before auto-PRs are enabled (controlled by ENG-4120).

Risks & Mitigations:
- Cache behavior changes can surface discrepancies: added 'ci/cache-keys.md' and explicit cache-version bumps.
- Automated dep PRs could group incompatible updates: dep-curator includes a staged matrix (oldest-supported X newest) and runs smoke e2e in a sandbox; failures block auto-PRs.

Files of interest (summary): .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/dep-curator.yml, build/profiles/ci.Dockerfile, build/profiles/release.Dockerfile, tools/dep-curator/action.yaml, tools/dep-curator/curator.py, scripts/toolchain_resolver.sh, docs/ci/dep-curation.md, build/profiles/README.md, Makefile, pkg/build/profile.md, tsconfig.json (minor), go.mod (module pinning hints).

Design notes: The build profiles aim to be explicit and minimal: 'minimal' is just enough to produce a static artifact for quick local iteration; 'ci' is tuned for consistent cache keys and hermetic toolchains; 'release' produces multi-arch artifacts and strips debugging info. Dep-curator is intentionally conservative: it groups semver-minor upgrades, treats semver-major as manual review, and uses a retry/opinionated rebase strategy to keep PR churn small.
